title: Microsoft Teams: onboarding workflow connects new team members to channels
summary: The briefing accurately reports both the roadmap target and the later rollout window given to tenant administrators. The membership controls and product-level licensing are supported, and independent searches found no documentation resolving the workflow-specific settings, default or licensing gaps.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Team membership can be managed at Teams admin center > Teams > Manage teams > team > Members.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, expand Teams and select Manage teams.
Select the team name under the display name column.
In the Members tab, you can add or remove members and assign owner and moderator roles to members.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Add-TeamUser -GroupId <team GroupId> -User <user principal name> to add a team member.
claims.quote:
Add-TeamUser
    -GroupId <String>
    -User <String>
    [-Role <String>]
GroupId of the team.
UPN of a user of the organization (user principal name - e.g. johndoe@example.com).
Default value: Member

claims.claim: Add-TeamUser adds a member to the team and its backing group rather than configuring channel settings.
claims.quote: This cmdlet adds an owner or member to the team, and to the unified group which backs the team.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether adding a member through the admin centre, PowerShell or group sync starts this workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "onboarding workflow" "Add-TeamUser" "sync". Opened Add-TeamUser and assign-roles-permissions; read teams-channels-overview membership excerpts. These describe team membership changes and sync but not their interaction with this workflow.

claims.claim: The Members-tab control presented in the table manages membership of the selected team, not configuration of the new onboarding workflow.
claims.quote:
